source: "Create a massive, floating stone arena inspired by the Dragon Ball Super Tournament of Power. The world is set in an infinite cosmic void with glowing nebulae, floating celestial platforms, shifting dimensional colors, and high-tech energy pillars surrounding the arena. Make the atmosphere feel boundless, hyper-cosmic, and transcendent with dramatic lighting."

answers.ask: Are the smaller floating platforms fightable ground, or backdrop only? Fighting on them makes this a multi-level arena and a slower build.
answers.answer: The smaller floating celestial platforms are backdrop only; keep all playable combat on the main floating stone arena.

answers.ask: Is the win condition ring-out, last-one-standing, or a timed tournament bracket?
answers.answer: Use ring-out as the win condition, matching the Tournament of Power-inspired arena.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] shape — Q: Are the smaller floating platforms fightable ground, or backdrop only? Fighting on them makes this a multi-level arena and a slower build. A: The smaller floating celestial platforms are backdrop only; keep all playable combat on the main floating stone arena.
- [author] goal — Q: Is the win condition ring-out, last-one-standing, or a timed tournament bracket? A: Use ring-out as the win condition, matching the Tournament of Power-inspired arena.
- [agent_inferred] arena surface — Q: Is the main arena tiered or flat? A: Use one broad flat combat floor because no playable elevation was requested.

## Enriched image prompt
Create a massive floating stone combat arena suspended in an infinite cosmic void, using an original hyper-cosmic design rather than copying a named franchise. Keep all playable ground on one broad flat collision-clean stone platform with open ring-out edges. Surround the arena with high-tech energy pillars, dramatic glowing nebulae, shifting dimensional colors, and smaller floating celestial platforms that remain distant backdrop only. Use dramatic transcendent lighting and a boundless composition while keeping the main arena surface visually dominant and completely readable.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Action (`action`), specifically a ring-out battleground.

## Shape and preset
Use `space-bounded`, interpreted as a single flat main combat platform whose open edge defines the clash space. Use the Battlegrounds preset, dropping `cover-los` because the author requests one readable main platform and places the energy pillars around it rather than across the fighting floor.

## Config requirements
Use `hazard-kill` for the open ring-out edge and bottomless cosmic void surrounding the playable platform. Use the drawn form of `spawn-protected` for set-back arrival pads around the inner perimeter. The high-tech energy pillars, nebulae, dimensional colors, and non-playable celestial platforms are scene-specific visual content.

## Layout requirements
For `spawn-protected`, place evenly distributed combat SpawnZone markers on the inner portion of the main platform, set back from the ring-out edge and outside immediate opposing sightlines. Place one free-text BoundaryZone ring-out detector just beyond the full arena edge. Do not place traversal, spawns, or objectives on the background platforms.

## Layout components
The build contains exactly one playable floating stone arena, a continuous open edge, an inner spawn band, and a surrounding ring of energy pillars. Smaller celestial platforms, nebulae, and the void create background depth but have no playable connections. The composition centres the main platform and leaves its entire collision-clean floor visible.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: the cosmic atmosphere and monumental arena appearance lead, and the simple flat plan can be derived afterward.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is large, driven by the explicitly massive combat platform while preserving the arena floor and pillar detail. The theme is original dark hyper-cosmic fantasy with glowing high technology and dramatic nebula light. Use `P0`; all play stays on one flat surface, and backdrop platforms do not create traversal layers or volumetric play.
